anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, reference designators D9 and D10 are drawn as pulse/isolation transformers (coupled-coil symbol with pins named 'Input', 'Output' and a 'GND' pin), inserted in-line between the isolated CAN transceivers U11 (CAN0) / U10 (CAN1) and the CAN0_P/CAN0_N and CAN1_P/CAN1_N nets that go to connectors J2/J13. No CDSOT23-SM712 (or any SM712-family) TVS diode array appears anywhere on the CAN lines; the only TVS arrays in the drawing are TPD4E1U06DCKR (Ethernet) and USBLC6 (USB).
anomalies.expected: The specification's component table states D9 and D10 are CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays placed across CAN0_P/N and CAN1_P/N for CAN-bus transient/ESD protection ('the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice'). Furthermore U10/U11 are already isolated CAN transceivers (VCC1/VCC2/GND1/GND2), so no external isolation transformer is intended on their CAN side.

evidence.quote: D9, D10 — CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays on CAN0_P/N, CAN1_P/N — CAN bus transient/ESD protection ... the netlist's CDSOT23-SM712 matches this documented choice.

CAN BUS sheet: 'D10' transformer symbol (pins Input/Output/GND) between U11 CANH/CANL and CAN0_P/CAN0_N; 'D9' transformer symbol between U10 CANH/CANL and CAN1_P/CAN1_N (CAN Interface A/B connectors J2/J13).

anomalies.impact: The CAN connectors J2/J13 lose the specified transient/ESD protection, and the transformer coupling blocks the DC common-mode/recessive bias that an isolated transceiver places on CANH/CANL, so the bus signalling to the Odrive controllers through J2/J13 would not work as intended and the lines are unprotected against ESD/burst.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended design at D9/D10: the schematic draws them as CAN isolation transformers inserted between the already-isolated transceivers U10/U11 and the CAN bus nets, whereas the specification defines D9/D10 as CDSOT23-SM712 TVS diode arrays providing CAN transient/ESD protection (which are absent from the drawing). This both removes the specified ESD protection and mis-couples the CAN lines.
